meta.name: GPU / Graphics Processors
meta.definition: GPUs are specialized parallel-processing chips originally built for rendering graphics, now central to gaming, professional visualization, data-center AI training/inference, autonomous vehicles and high-performance computing.

summary.headline: India's GPU market is valued at roughly USD 5.7-6.0 billion in 2026 (Mordor Intelligence/Ken Research), growing at a India-leading 18-32% CAGR, as AI compute demand, the IndiaAI Mission's 34,000+ empanelled GPUs, and gaming/enterprise adoption outpace global growth of ~15%, even as India remains almost entirely import-dependent on NVIDIA, AMD and Intel silicon.
key_takeaways: India's GPU market size is estimated between USD 5.72 billion (Research & Markets, 2026) and USD 5,980 million (Ken Research, 2025), with forecasts to reach USD 13.97-31.3 billion by 2031, growing 18-32% CAGR - the fastest among Asian peers including China (22.4% CAGR) and Japan (17.8% CAGR).

India is 90-95% import-dependent for semiconductors including GPUs, spending near USD 150 billion cumulatively on imports FY17-FY25; discrete GPU boards attract 7.5-15% customs duty plus 18% GST, pushing retail prices 15-20% above global MSRPs.

The IndiaAI Mission has empanelled over 38,000 GPUs (targeting 63,000 by 2027 and up to 200,000 eventually) at subsidized rates as low as ₹65-115 per hour, with NVIDIA H100/H200 and AMD MI300-series as approved architectures, run through 14 empanelled providers including Yotta, CyFuture, Netmagic and Sify.

NVIDIA dominates India's discrete/AI GPU landscape with a leading position and holds ~92% of the global AI/data-center and AIB GPU market; AMD has lifted its India datacenter footprint to roughly 20-25% of deployments, while Intel's Gaudi 3 is signing India customers like Airtel, Infosys and Ola Krutrim.

Data center/AI/HPC use is fast overtaking gaming as the growth engine - enterprise-grade GPUs are expected to exceed half of India's GPU revenue by 2030 (up from 35-40% in 2026), even though gaming still leads unit shipments and India has 560-591 million gamers, the world's largest base.
summary.report_markdown:
## Market Size & Growth
India's GPU market is sized between **USD 5.72 billion (2026, Research & Markets)** and **USD 5,980 million (2025, Ken Research)**, having grown from just USD 1,130 million in 2018 and USD 2,032 million in 2020. Forecasts diverge but agree on rapid expansion: Research & Markets projects USD 13.97 billion by 2031 (19.6% CAGR), Ken Research projects USD 31,276 million by 2031 (31.75% CAGR - the highest among Asia-Pacific peers versus China's 22.4% and Japan's 17.8%), and Credence Research projects USD 10.4 billion by 2032 (18.58% CAGR). The India discrete GPU sub-segment alone is pegged at USD 3.73 billion in 2026, rising to USD 9.33 billion by 2031 (20.15% CAGR). Globally the GPU market is estimated at USD 128-145 billion in 2025-26, on track toward USD 237-1,712 billion by the early-to-mid 2030s depending on the source, with Asia-Pacific holding 43% of global revenue.

## Segments
By **product form**, discrete GPUs hold 63.84-66.18% of India's GPU market versus 33.82% for integrated GPUs (2025); servers/data-center accelerators lead device application with 38.6% share, reflecting the AI-driven shift. By **application**, gaming leads India's application mix (largest single category) followed by data centers, AI/ML, video editing and visualization, though enterprise AI compute already contributes over 38% of India GPU revenue in 2026. By **region**, North India leads with 30% share (Delhi NCR data centers), South India follows at 28% (Bengaluru/Hyderabad tech investment), West India at 25% and East India at 17%; separately, five metro clusters (Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai, Pune) account for ~60% of GPU sales.

## Value Chain & Import Dependence
India has **no sub-28nm fabrication capability**, so all advanced datacenter GPUs (4nm and below) must be imported; GPUs represent roughly 90% of an AI server's bill of materials. Over 85% of India's GPU unit supply is sourced from overseas assembly hubs in China (55-65% of import value), Taiwan (15-20%) and Vietnam (5-10%). Nearly 90-95% of India's total semiconductor demand is met via imports, with India spending ~USD 150 billion cumulatively on semiconductor imports FY17-FY25 (23% CAGR) - a trajectory that could reach USD 240 billion/year by 2035 if unchecked. Global upstream chokepoints matter directly to India: TSMC controls 60-65% of leading-edge foundry capacity, Samsung and SK Hynix supply the HBM stacks used in AI GPUs, and ASML is the sole supplier of the most advanced lithography tools. Domestic GPU board assembly (Noida, Bengaluru, Chennai, Pune) exists but adds only 15-25% value to the finished board, covering an estimated 40-55% of domestic unit demand; Tata Electronics' USD 11 billion Dholera fab (targeting 50,000 wafer starts/month) is India's first attempt at building fab capacity, expected online around 2028.

## Duties, Tariffs & Trade Policy
Finished GPU boards (HS 8473.30/85439000) attract 7.5-15% basic customs duty, 18% IGST and a 10% social welfare surcharge, pushing landed cost premiums of 25-35% and retail prices 15-20% above global MSRP. BIS registration and end-user certification (aligned with the Wassenaar Arrangement for dual-use high-compute GPUs) add 4-12 weeks to procurement cycles and cost INR 1-3 lakh per SKU. Geopolitically, India is treated as a 'Tier 2' country under US AI Diffusion export-control rules and has historically faced a roughly 50,000-GPU cap on high-end chip imports from the US, a constraint reportedly being eased as part of ongoing India-US trade talks; the broader US-China tariff war (peaking near 145% on Chinese goods in April 2025) and US export controls on China have redirected global chip-industry attention and created both risk and opportunity for India as an alternative sourcing/assembly base.

## Government Push: IndiaAI Mission
Approved in March 2024 with a ₹10,372 crore (~USD 1.21-1.36 billion) outlay, the IndiaAI Mission has built a national GPU compute pool that crossed **34,333 GPUs** in mid-2025 and **38,000+ GPUs** by end-2025, with government targets of 63,000 GPUs by 2027 and ambitions floated for 100,000-200,000 GPUs. Seven empanelled bidders (CyFuture, Yotta, Locuz, Sify, Netmagic, Vensysco, Ishan Infotech) supply subsidized on-demand GPU access (NVIDIA H100/H200/B200, AMD MI300X/MI325X) at rates as low as ₹65-115/hour versus a global benchmark of ₹213-256/hour, with a further 40% discount for startups, academia and students. Domestically, India is targeting "tech-demo-ready" indigenous GPUs by end-2025 and production by 2029.

## Players
Globally the industry is an oligopoly - NVIDIA, AMD and Intel dominate, with NVIDIA holding ~92% of the discrete/AIB and AI/data-center GPU market. In India, NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Qualcomm and AWS are named as the top five players, with NVIDIA holding clear market leadership across gaming, AI and data center. Domestic cloud/compute providers (Yotta Data Services, NxtGen, E2E Networks, CyFuture, Netmagic, Sify) build India-based GPU infrastructure atop imported silicon; AIB partners (ASUS, Gigabyte, MSI, Zotac, Sapphire, Palit) compete on service and warranty in the India retail channel, while distributors Ingram Micro India, Redington, Savex and Rashi Peripherals control 55-65% of organized GPU imports. Grey-market/parallel imports still account for an estimated 15-20% of India's consumer GPU sales.

## Headwinds & Tailwinds
Tailwinds include AI/data-center demand (enterprise GPU CAGR of 18-22% vs 8-12% for consumer), a huge 560-591 million-strong gaming base, government subsidy/PLI support, and hyperscaler capex (Microsoft USD 17.5bn, Google USD 15bn pledged for India 2026-2030). Headwinds include near-total import dependence, 25-35% landed-cost duty premiums, INR depreciation (INR 82 to 85/USD) adding 3-4% to invoices, US export-control uncertainty, global DRAM/HBM price spikes (DRAM up 171.8% YoY) squeezing GPU supply and pricing, and power infrastructure deficits in tier-2/3 cities limiting high-end GPU deployment.

sections.heading: Executive summary
prose: India's GPU market is valued at roughly USD 5.72 billion in 2026, according to Research & Markets, up from USD 4.93 billion in 2025 and just USD 1.13 billion in 2018. Ken Research puts 2025 value even higher, near USD 5,980 million. Either way, the market is growing fast, forecast to reach USD 13.97 billion by 2031 on a 19.55% CAGR (Research & Markets) or as high as 31.75% CAGR (Ken Research) - a pace that outstrips China (22.4%) and Japan (17.8%).

Growth is driven by two forces: a surging domestic AI compute build-out anchored by the government's IndiaAI Mission, and a gaming/consumer base that is the largest in the world by user count. At the same time, India remains almost entirely dependent on imported silicon from NVIDIA, AMD, Intel and others, since it has no domestic fabrication below 28nm. This import dependence, combined with duties and a weakening rupee, keeps retail GPU prices well above global levels.

sections.heading: Market size & growth
prose: India's GPU market stood at USD 5.72 billion in 2026, per Research & Markets, following USD 4.93 billion in 2025 and USD 4.5 billion in 2024. The market has grown steadily from USD 1.13 billion in 2018, through USD 2.032 billion (2020), USD 2.401 billion (2021), USD 2.868 billion (2022) and USD 3.503 billion (2023). Forecasts point to USD 13.97 billion by 2031, implying a CAGR of about 19.55% for 2026-2031. Ken Research's separate estimate is more aggressive, projecting a 31.75% CAGR to 2031.
This growth rate places India ahead of other major Asian GPU markets, with China growing at 22.4% CAGR and Japan at 17.8% CAGR over similar forecast periods.

sections.heading: Segments
prose: Discrete GPUs made up 66.18% of India's GPU market in 2025, favored for their superior gaming, AI and data-center performance. Integrated GPUs held the remaining 33.82% but dominate unit shipments in mainstream laptops and smartphones. Within the discrete GPU market, servers and data-center accelerators are the leading application, accounting for 38.62% of the segment in 2025 - ahead of gaming, which still leads the overall India GPU market by application when measured across all device categories.

Regionally, North India leads with 30% market share, driven by Delhi NCR's data-center growth and IT hubs. South India follows with 28%, powered by tech investment in Bengaluru and Hyderabad. West India holds 25%, supported by financial services and smart-city initiatives, while East India accounts for 17%, showing steady growth in digital infrastructure and cloud adoption.

sections.heading: Value chain
prose: The value chain starts with wafer fabrication, concentrated with TSMC, Samsung and Intel; TSMC alone commands 60-65% of leading-edge foundry capacity, and India has no domestic capability at these nodes. Memory supply - HBM and GDDR - comes from Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron, who allocate early HBM volumes to the largest cloud buyers first, constraining supply for smaller India-based firms. GDDR remains attractive for mid-tier cards due to a cost gap of USD 500-1,000 per GPU versus HBM.

NVIDIA and AMD operate as fabless designers, outsourcing manufacturing to TSMC and Samsung, while Intel is vertically integrated. Domestic assembly in India - centered in Noida, Bengaluru, Chennai and Pune, led by EMS players Dixon Technologies, VVDN and Syrma SGS under the PLI scheme - adds only 15-25% of the finished board's value, since dies and key components are imported.

Distribution runs through top-tier importers like Ingram Micro India, Redington, Savex and Rashi Peripherals, who together control 55-65% of organized GPU imports; import duty and GST add 25-35% to landed cost before distributor margins. On the deployment side, cloud providers such as Yotta, NxtGen, E2E Networks, Jio and AdaniConneX install imported GPUs in India data centers, where power-related expenses eat up nearly 75% of operating costs.

key_numbers.label: Power cost share of data-center opex

sections.heading: Distribution & channels
prose: Top-tier authorized distributors - Ingram Micro India, Redington, Savex Technologies and Rashi Peripherals - control an estimated 60% of organized GPU imports into India. E-commerce platforms including Amazon India, Flipkart, and specialized retailers like MD Computers and Vedant Computers serve consumer and prosumer buyers.
Grey-market and parallel-import channels remain significant, accounting for an estimated 17.5% (range 15-20%) of consumer GPU sales, which undermines organized retail and warranty support.

sections.heading: Key players & positioning
prose: NVIDIA is the dominant force in India's discrete and AI GPU market, holding about 92% of the global discrete/AIB and AI/data-center GPU market as of Q3 2025. AMD has raised its India data-center footprint to roughly 20-25% of deployments in 2025 as it targets emerging markets. Intel's Gaudi 3 accelerator, which claims 50% better throughput than NVIDIA's H100 on some benchmarks, has signed India customers including Airtel, Infosys and Ola Krutrim. Qualcomm and Amazon Web Services round out the top five players, with Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 delivering a 23% graphics uplift for on-device generative AI.

India's IndiaAI Mission has empanelled 14 compute providers, including Yotta Data Services, CyFuture, Netmagic, Sify, Locuz, Vensysco and Ishan Infotech, who won competitive bids (L1 status) across NVIDIA A100/H100/H200, AMD MI300X and AWS Inferentia2/Trainium categories. Yotta operates the largest known India GPU fleet, deploying over 16,384 NVIDIA H100 GPUs at its Navi Mumbai NM1 facility and placing a USD 2 billion order for 20,736 NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra modules.

Other notable participants include E2E Networks, which supplies NVIDIA Hopper GPUs to clients like AI4Bharat and has commissioned H200 clusters in Delhi NCR and Chennai; NxtGen, which is expanding with liquid-cooled H200, MI325x and B300 GPUs in Karnataka; and Jio Platforms and Tata Communications, both active in India's GPU procurement tenders. In add-in-board retail, ASUS is seen as the 'gold standard' for build quality and repair service, Zotac is the 'value king' due to its five-year warranty, Gigabyte is improving its reputation with a dedicated India engineering team, and MSI is favored for design but criticized for weak post-warranty support. Netweb Technologies has partnered with NVIDIA to manufacture AI/HPC servers in India, including Grace CPU and GH200 Superchip designs.

sections.heading: Supply & capacity
prose: India's national GPU compute pool under the IndiaAI Mission has reached 38,000 GPUs, up from an initial target of just 10,000, with plans to expand to 63,000 by 2027 and potentially 200,000 eventually. Yotta Data Services is scaling its Navi Mumbai facilities toward a roadmap of 32,768 NVIDIA H100 GPUs by end-2025. On the manufacturing side, Tata Electronics is building a fab in Dholera, Gujarat targeting 50,000 wafer starts per month by 2028, though this does not yet address leading-edge GPU nodes.

Annual GPU import value into India is estimated at USD 1.8-2.5 billion in 2026, growing 12-16% per year, underscoring the country's continued reliance on external supply even as domestic compute deployment scales up.

sections.heading: Tailwinds vs headwinds
prose: India's growth tailwinds include rising internet penetration - 50%, over 700 million users in 2024 - and a GPU market CAGR forecast (31.75%) that outpaces China (22.4%) and Japan (17.8%). US-India trade talks reportedly include easing the roughly 50,000-unit GPU import cap that had constrained access to top-end NVIDIA and AMD chips. Notebook shipments climbed 8.1% year-over-year in Q1 2025, led by gaming laptops, supporting discrete-GPU demand.

Headwinds are substantial. India lacks sub-28nm fabrication, so all advanced datacenter GPUs (4nm and below) must be imported, exposing the market to overseas foundry allocation decisions. Currency depreciation from INR 82 to INR 85 per USD by early 2026 adds another 3-4% to import invoices, on top of import duty structures that already add 20-35% to landed costs, with BIS/end-user-certification compliance adding 4-12 weeks to procurement. Power infrastructure deficits, especially in tier-2/3 grids, are estimated to drag India's discrete GPU CAGR forecast by -2.8%. Globally, DRAM prices are up 171.8% year-over-year, and HBM allocation bias toward AI hyperscalers is constraining supply and raising prices for India buyers. Grey-market and parallel-import channels account for an estimated 15-20% of consumer GPU sales, undermining organized retail.

key_numbers.label: Import duty impact on landed cost

sections.heading: Outlook
prose: India's GPU market is set to keep growing faster than most of the world, with forecasts ranging from a 19.55% CAGR (Research & Markets, to USD 13.97 billion by 2031) to a steeper 31.75% CAGR (Ken Research). This growth will be increasingly driven by enterprise and data-center demand, which is expanding at 18-22% CAGR through 2030, versus 8-12% for the consumer segment - enterprise GPUs are expected to exceed half of India's GPU revenue by 2030, up from 35-40% in 2026.

Government programs will remain central: the IndiaAI Mission's push toward 63,000 empanelled GPUs by 2027, Semicon India 2.0's INR 76,000 crore (USD 9.1 billion) in incentives, and hyperscaler capital commitments - Microsoft's USD 17.5 billion and Google's USD 15 billion through 2026-2030 - will keep lifting domestic GPU deployment. But structural headwinds - import dependence for leading-edge silicon, currency depreciation, duty structures, power infrastructure gaps, and global memory price pressure - mean India's growth will continue to run on imported technology rather than domestic manufacturing for the foreseeable future.
